title: Introduction to Algorithms
author: Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest, Stein
subject: Algorithms
description: Covers a broad range of algorithms in depth while keeping the design and analysis readable for students. Each chapter works as a standalone unit of study and every algorithm is presented with pseudocode, worked examples and complexity analysis.

reviews.text: Best reference for DSA prep. Dense, but the explanations are extremely thorough.
Heavy read. Still a must-have for anyone preparing for placement interviews.

title: Clean Code
author: Robert C. Martin
subject: Coding Practices
description: A practical guide to writing readable, maintainable code. Built around before-and-after case studies that show how small naming and structure decisions add up across a real codebase.

reviews.text: Changed how I name variables and split functions. Very easy to read in one weekend.

title: Linear Algebra and Its Applications
author: Gilbert Strang
subject: Linear Algebra
description: Builds linear algebra from vectors and matrices up to eigenvalues and singular value decomposition, with an applied focus that connects well to machine learning and graphics coursework.

reviews.text: Strang explains intuition first and proofs second. Helped a lot with the ML elective.

title: Operating System Concepts
author: Silberschatz, Galvin, Gagne
subject: Operating Systems
description: The standard OS textbook. Covers processes, threads, CPU scheduling, deadlocks, memory management and file systems, with case studies on Linux and Windows.

reviews.text: The dinosaur book. Scheduling and deadlock chapters are the most useful for exams.

title: Computer Networks
author: Andrew S. Tanenbaum
subject: Networking
description: Walks the network stack layer by layer, from the physical layer up to application protocols, with plenty of real protocol examples rather than abstract theory.

title: Database System Concepts
author: Silberschatz, Korth, Sudarshan
subject: Databases
description: Covers relational design, SQL, normalization, transaction management and indexing. The normalization and transaction chapters map directly onto the DBMS lab syllabus.

reviews.text: Normalization finally made sense after the worked examples in chapter 8.

title: Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications
author: Kenneth H. Rosen
subject: Discrete Mathematics
description: Standard discrete maths text covering logic, proofs, counting, graphs and trees. Large exercise sets at the end of every section make it good for practice.

title: Compilers: Principles and Techniques
author: Aho, Lam, Sethi, Ullman
subject: Compiler Design
description: The dragon book. Takes a source program all the way through lexical analysis, parsing, semantic analysis, optimisation and code generation.

reviews.text: Parsing chapters are dense but the worked grammar examples are worth it.

title: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach
author: Russell and Norvig
subject: Artificial Intelligence
description: Broad survey of AI, from search and logic through probabilistic reasoning and learning. Works both as a course text and as a reference for the AI elective project.

reviews.text: Search algorithms chapter helped directly with the AI lab assignment.

title: Design Patterns
author: Gamma, Helm, Johnson, Vlissides
subject: Design Patterns
description: The original catalogue of 23 object-oriented design patterns, each with intent, structure, participants and sample code.

title: Deep Learning
author: Goodfellow, Bengio, Courville
subject: Machine Learning
description: Maths-heavy introduction to deep learning, starting from linear algebra and probability before moving into feedforward networks, regularisation and sequence models.

title: Learning React
author: A. Banks and E. Porcello
subject: Web Development
description: Hooks-first introduction to React covering components, state, effects and routing. Useful reference for Phase 4 of this project when the pages move to React.
